title: Livepeer registry manifest
description: Top-level wrapper plus signed manifest content. Published at /.well-known/livepeer-registry.json by the orch-coordinator. Signature is computed by the cold key on secure-orch over the canonical (RFC 8785 JCS) form of the manifest payload.

public_key.description: Uncompressed secp256k1 public key, hex, 65 bytes (0x04 || X || Y). Same curve as the manifest signature, so a consumer verifies settlement with the primitives it already has.

not_before.description: Start of the key's validity window.

expires_at.description: End of the key's validity window. An outgoing key stays listed until this passes so a record signed just before a rotation still verifies — without the overlap, rotating a key would invalidate settlements already in flight.

spec_version.description: Spec-wide SemVer (major.minor or major.minor.patch). Consumers MUST validate the major version; minor and patch are non-breaking by definition. See livepeer-network-protocol/VERSION.

publication_seq.description: Strictly-increasing publication counter. Each cold-key signature emits a value greater than every previously-signed value for this orch's eth_address. Resolvers cache the last-seen value per eth_address and reject manifests with publication_seq <= last_seen. Defends against rollback within the (issued_at, expires_at) validity window.

issued_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp at which the orch's cold key signed this manifest.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp after which consumers MUST refetch. Resolvers MUST NOT route on expired manifests.

settlement_keys.description: Hot keys the orch's cold key delegates settlement signing to. A broker is network-exposed, so it must never hold the cold key that anchors the operator's on-chain identity; it signs settlement records with one of these instead. Consumers accept a record signed by any listed key whose validity window contains the record's issued_at, which is what makes rotation an ordinary republish: publish a manifest with the new key, a higher publication_seq, and the outgoing key still present until its expires_at.

capabilities.description: Flat list of capability tuples. Host is not a registration unit; multi-binary or multi-broker hosts contribute multiple entries here.

eth_address.description: The orch's on-chain identity (Arbitrum One). Signature MUST recover to this address.

service_uri.description: Optional. Diagnostic URL where this manifest is hosted. SHOULD match the on-chain ServiceRegistry entry but is not authoritative; the on-chain entry is the trust anchor.

capability_id.description: Opaque UTF-8 identifier. No closed enum; orchs and gateways may invent new ones (see core belief #1, #7).

offering_id.description: Opaque UTF-8 identifier disambiguating priced tiers under the capability (e.g. different models, hardware classes, SLAs).

protocol.description: Protocol tag, e.g. 'paid-job/v1' or 'paid-session/v1'. Protocol specs live in protocols/<name>.md. Consumers MUST refuse unknown protocols, never guess. Declared axes ride in the matching 'job' or 'session' object (see protocols/offering-axes.md).

price_per_unit_wei.description: Wei per `per_units` work units, expressed as a non-negative decimal string. String form preserves precision beyond JSON's safe-integer range. Read with per_units, never alone: this is the price of a batch of units, not necessarily of one.

per_units.description: Denominator of price_per_unit_wei: the price buys this many work units. Absent means 1. Lets an offering price below 1 wei per unit, which token-metered workloads need. Every layer that carries the price MUST carry this with it — see protocols/offering-axes.md §6, which also fixes the cumulative ceiling billing rule both payer and payee compute.

worker_url.description: Public TLS endpoint of the broker (or any operator-chosen public-facing proxy that fronts it). MUST be HTTPS. NAT traversal / tunneling is the orch's concern (cloudflared, Traefik, etc.).

extra.description: Orch-declared metadata. Free-form key-value pairs. Gateways use these for workload-specific filtering (region, GPU class, latency tier, etc.). The protocol itself does not interpret extra.

constraints.description: Gateway-side filter hints. Same shape as extra; semantics are gateway-defined.

transports.description: Transports this offering serves. Selected per-request by HTTP negotiation; brokers refuse undeclared transports before payment side effects.

descriptor_schema.description: Runtime-descriptor schema tag (protocols/runtime-descriptor.md). Gateways MUST NOT open sessions whose schema they do not implement; brokers reject runner descriptors that do not match it.

attachment.description: 'external': runtime coordinates come from the descriptor; data never transits the broker. 'inband-ws': the data plane is a broker-relayed WebSocket.

metering.description: Origin of the seller's usage claims. 'broker-observed' is valid only with attachment 'inband-ws' — a broker cannot observe traffic that never transits it.

max_rotations.description: Cap on how many times a session may be rebound onto a rotated payment identity (protocols/paid-session.md §3.3.1). Absent or 0 means the default, 3. Consumers gate on nothing here; it is the broker's own bound, advertised so an operator can see it. Note a 'bounded' offering cannot survive a rotation at all — its successor identity starts at a zero balance.

refill.description: 'bounded' offerings reject top-up after open. The clearinghouse gates refill on this field.

lease.description: Lease policy override; absent means the session spec's normative funding-tracking default.

tolerance_band_pct.description: Advisory: divergence tolerance the seller commits to operate within (trust-model doc). Buyers may prefer tighter bands at route selection.

runway_increment_units.description: Advisory: seller-suggested top-up sizing. Buyers own their actual increment; it is their exposure bound.

session_params_schema.description: Opaque description of the session_params this capability expects, as declared by the runner (paid-session/v1 §7.1.1). Relayed verbatim to gateways so they can validate before opening rather than discovering the requirement as a create-time failure. Never enforced by the broker or the registry — the runner remains the authority on its own inputs.

name.description: The metering dimension's name, e.g. 'tokens', 'video-frame-megapixel', 'barks'. Opaque to the protocol; consumed by gateways for billing display. The extractor (which counts the units) is host-config concern, not advertised here.

signature.title: Cold-key signature
signature.description: Signature is computed over the JCS-canonicalized (RFC 8785) form of the manifest payload. Signers: the orch's cold key on secure-orch.

algorithm.description: Signing algorithm. Currently only secp256k1 (Ethereum's curve) is permitted, matching the orch's on-chain identity.

value.description: Hex-encoded signature bytes. For secp256k1: 65 bytes (r || s || v) where v is 27 or 28.

canonicalization.description: JSON canonicalization scheme used before hashing. JCS = RFC 8785.
